name: Combo Chain
description: The grammar of offense: which move may cancel into which, inside what frame window, plus the input buffer and motion-input recognition (quarter-circles, dragon punches) that make intent legible at fighting-game speed. It owns the chain table and the buffer because both answer the same question — 'what did the player mean, and are they allowed to do it now' — and splitting them produces the classic bug where a buffered input fires a move the cancel rules would have forbidden. It deliberately does not own contact: combat.hitbox_hurtbox reports combat.hit_confirmed, and a cancel window opens on confirmed hits (hit-confirming) rather than on button presses, which is what separates real chains from mash-friendly animation blending. It also does not own damage scaling; scaling on chain depth is combat.damage_resolver's knob, fed by the step count this publishes.

inputs.name: chainTable
inputs.description: Entries of {fromMove, toMove, windowFrames, cancelType}. The table is the character: two fighters with identical moves but different tables play nothing alike.

inputs.name: inputBufferFrames
inputs.description: How long an input is remembered before it expires. Eight frames forgives early presses without letting players queue whole strings blindly.

inputs.name: cancelWindowFrames
inputs.description: Default window after a confirmed hit during which a legal cancel is accepted, used when a chain entry does not override it.

inputs.name: motionInputTable
inputs.description: Direction sequences that read as special motions, with per-motion leniency. Leniency is per motion because a quarter-circle and a 360 deserve different mercy.

inputs.name: dropResetFrames
inputs.description: Frames without a confirmed hit before the chain resets to neutral. Long enough to survive a whiffed linker, short enough that a dropped combo cannot be resurrected.
